results.content: # **SimCLR** and NT-Xent Loss Explained. Because these augmented views are still raw pixels, we feed them into an encoder ***f*** (ResNet in the original paper) to obtain representations ***h***. First, identify positive pairs — representations originating from the same source image. 1. Compute cosine similarity between **i** and every other representation in the batch (total **2N − 1** scores). ## How to Evaluate SimCLR-trained Representations? How should we judge the quality of representations learned by SimCLR? In the original paper, ImageNet serves for training and evaluation. For linear probing, we freeze the entire SimCLR-trained vision backbone (ResNet). This protocol isolates representation quality from the task-specific head, letting us compare SimCLR with other unsupervised or semi-supervised methods on the same protocol. The following figure contrasts SimCLR with contemporary self-supervised approaches under linear evaluation. Semi-supervised learning sits between self-supervised and fully supervised regimes: we use a small labeled subset while most data remain unlabeled. After SimCLR pre-training, we leave **all** backbone and classifier weights trainable, select either **1 % or 10 %** of ImageNet as labeled data, and fine-tune the entire network on that small subset. The next figure reports SimCLR’s performance against other self-supervised methods of the time under semi-supervised fine-tuning. Starting from SimCLR pre-trained weights, we evaluate on datasets such as CIFAR-10/100, Caltech-101, Cars, Pets, and Flowers. As before, we can either freeze the backbone and train a new head or train the whole model on each new target dataset. The original paper tests SimCLR across 12 datasets. The next figure compares its transfer performance to standard supervised training. And SimCLR with the entire model fine-tuned, outperforms the supervised baseline on five datasets. ## Other Methods to Learn Visual Representations. The first trains a model to re-generate images pixel-by-pixel; the second builds a heuristic-driven task, compels the model to learn meaningful representations. A previous work *“Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning by Context Prediction”*trains the model to guess a patch’s position relative to another. Methods such as InfoNCE frame representation learning as a prediction task between positive and negative examples. (I’ve covered InfoNCE in a separate post.) And SimCLR is one of the most influential methods in this family.

results.title: [2304.13089] Objectives Matter: Understanding the Impact of Self-Supervised Objectives on Vision Transformer Representations
results.content: [Submitted on 25 Apr 2023]. # Title:Objectives Matter: Understanding the Impact of Self-Supervised Objectives on Vision Transformer Representations. View a PDF of the paper titled Objectives Matter: Understanding the Impact of Self-Supervised Objectives on Vision Transformer Representations, by Shashank Shekhar and 3 other authors. > Abstract:Joint-embedding based learning (e.g., SimCLR, MoCo, DINO) and reconstruction-based learning (e.g., BEiT, SimMIM, MAE) are the two leading paradigms for self-supervised learning of vision transformers, but they differ substantially in their transfer performance. Here, we aim to explain these differences by analyzing the impact of these objectives on the structure and transferability of the learned representations. Our analysis reveals that reconstruction-based learning features are significantly dissimilar to joint-embedding based learning features and that models trained with similar objectives learn similar features even across architectures. We find that joint-embedding features yield better linear probe transfer for classification because the different objectives drive different distributions of information and invariances in the learned representation. These differences explain opposite trends in transfer performance for downstream tasks that require spatial specificity in features. Finally, we address how fine-tuning changes reconstructive representations to enable better transfer, showing that fine-tuning re-organizes the information to be more similar to pre-trained joint embedding models. **[v1]** Tue, 25 Apr 2023 18:48:23 UTC (10,419 KB). ## Access Paper:.
